title: A Novel Adaptive Cluster-Based Normalization Approach for MCDM Under Uncertainty: A Case Study on International Logistics Supplier Evaluation Under Industry 4.0
tldr: Proposes an adaptive cluster-based normalization method for TOPSIS MCDM that improves accuracy in logistics supplier evaluation under uncertainty.
problem_and_motivation: Supplier selection is critical for logistics success. Multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) faces the challenge of selecting an appropriate normalization method, as traditional approaches like Maximum, Sum, Vector, and Max-Min normalization each have limitations. The absence of a robust normalization method can lead to less precise decisions and significant economic losses for companies. Existing normalization methods either compress scores too much or produce negative values that create ambiguity in interpretation.
approach: Developed a novel adaptive cluster-based normalization approach that uses k-means clustering (k=3) to group criteria scores.
Applied cluster-based normalization using mean and standard deviation of each cluster rather than global maximum or sum.
Integrated the method with TOPSIS decision-making framework.
Tested on international logistics supplier evaluation for agricultural products in the wine industry under Industry 4.0 and digitalization context.
Compared normalization performance against Maximum, Sum, Vector, and Max-Min methods using normalized performance ratio, entropy, and Gini coefficient metrics.
findings: Traditional normalization methods showed significant variation in results — Maximum normalization gave supplier 10 the highest ranking while Sum normalization ranked it last.
Adaptive normalization produced a consistent pattern of results with smaller variation (standard deviation 0.015) and more balanced distribution among suppliers.
Adaptive normalization outperformed traditional methods in terms of normalized performance ratio, entropy, and Gini coefficient.
Suppliers 3, 4, and 8 ranked highest across all normalization methods due to strong technical support and competitive pricing.
Suppliers 10 and 12 ranked consistently lowest due to long lead times, poor communication, low innovation, and weak digital presence.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces a novel adaptive cluster-based normalization approach for TOPSIS that addresses the problem of inconsistent results from traditional normalization methods. By grouping criteria values using k-means clustering before normalization, the method produces more balanced distributions and reduces result variability. The case study in international logistics supplier evaluation demonstrates that traditional methods can produce contradictory rankings, while the adaptive method produces consistent results. The paper provides a practical contribution to MCDM methodology that could be applied to financial decision-making contexts where criteria have diverse scales.
directly_justifies: Traditional normalization methods in MCDM can produce contradictory results depending on which method is used.
Cluster-based normalization using k-means with k=3 produces more balanced and consistent distributions.
The adaptive method outperforms traditional methods on normalized performance ratio, entropy, and Gini coefficient metrics.
Suppliers with strong technical support and competitive pricing consistently rank highest across all normalization methods.
